module purpose: neorv32_uart is a bus-controlled UART that stores control settings, writes transmit bytes into a TX FIFO and serializes them to uart_txd_o, samples uart_rxd_i into an RX FIFO, and reports status, interrupts, clock-generator enable, and a flow-control output.

use-case flows.value: control-register fields written from the bus: enable, simulation-mode bit, hardware-flow-control enable, prescaler, baud divider, interrupt enables, and RX/TX clear strobes
selected clock-generator tap and baud divider pace UART transmit and receive bit timing
bus-written transmit data is queued and shifted onto the serial output
serial input samples are synchronized, assembled into a received byte, and pushed into the RX FIFO
TX and RX interrupt requests generated from configured FIFO conditions
receive-overrun status set when a new received byte arrives while the RX FIFO is full
outgoing flow-control decision driven from hardware-flow-control mode and RX FIFO fill level
control/status bits and received data returned on bus_rsp_o.data
control bits, IRQ outputs, UART engine state, overrun flag, and flow-control output forced to reset values while rstn_i='0'

conceptual assets.reasoning: The configure flow writes ctrl.enable at line 179. That held bit is read back at line 195, exported on clkgen_en_o at line 228, clears both FIFOs when deasserted (lines 259 and 304), gates both interrupt outputs (lines 270 and 315), and is copied into the TX/RX engine state vectors (lines 344 and 417). Integrity matters because corruption changes whether the UART runs and whether queued data is retained; availability is also established because the bit is held until rewritten and leaves the entity on clkgen_en_o.

conceptual assets.concept: UART bit-timing settings and derived tick
conceptual assets.reasoning: The configure flow writes ctrl.prsc and ctrl.baud at lines 182-183. ctrl.prsc selects which clkgen_i bit becomes uart_clk at line 229, and ctrl.baud is loaded into the TX and RX baud counters at lines 349, 368, 422, and 432; the transmit and receive engines only advance on uart_clk at lines 358, 366, 409, and 430. Integrity matters because wrong settings or a wrong selected tick break serialization and sampling cadence; availability is established because the settings are held until rewritten and the selected tick is recomputed whenever ctrl.prsc changes.

The configure flow writes ctrl.hwfc_en at line 181. The held bit qualifies transmitter release from wait at line 359 and selects whether uart_rtsn_o follows RX FIFO state or is forced low at lines 472-480. Integrity matters because corruption changes whether CTS/RTS throttling participates in UART operation; availability is established because the setting is held until rewritten.

The configure flow stores ctrl.irq_rx_nempty, ctrl.irq_rx_half, ctrl.irq_rx_full, ctrl.irq_tx_empty, and ctrl.irq_tx_nhalf at lines 185-189. Those held bits are then used to form irq_tx_o at lines 271-272 and irq_rx_o at lines 316-318, and they are also returned on control readback at lines 208-212. Integrity matters because wrong bits change which FIFO conditions assert interrupt requests; availability is established because the settings persist until rewritten.

conceptual assets.concept: RX and TX FIFO clear commands
conceptual assets.reasoning: Each cycle the bus process clears ctrl.clr_rx and ctrl.clr_tx to '0' (lines 173-174) and, on a control write, reloads them from bus_req_i.data (lines 190-191). Those strobes directly drive the RX and TX FIFO clear conditions at lines 304 and 259. Integrity matters because corruption wrongly discards or preserves queued data; availability is also established because a written clear command is held long enough to reach the FIFO clear logic.

The transmitter case on tx_engine.state (line 345) selects load, wait, shift, and idle behavior; tx_engine.baudcnt and tx_engine.bitcnt are loaded at lines 349-350 and updated at lines 368-372 and 369; tx_engine.cts samples the external flow-control input at line 337 and gates the wait-to-shift transition at line 359. The transmit operate flow depends on these stored states to fetch FIFO data, respect CTS when hardware flow control is enabled, pace bit times, and decide completion at lines 375-377, establishing integrity and conditional availability.

tx_engine.sreg loads FIFO output plus an appended '0' at line 351, shifts right with '1' insertion at line 370, and its current LSB drives tx_engine.txd at line 365, which leaves the entity on uart_txd_o at line 392. Because the bus request port is a transport record and the FIFO internals are in an unseen sub-unit, this shift register and the serial output port are the visible realization here. Integrity matters because wrong contents produce wrong serial bits; availability is conditional on tx_fifo.avail, ctrl.enable, uart_clk, and the CTS/hardware-flow-control guard (lines 352, 344, 358-359, 366-373).

rx_engine.sync samples uart_rxd_i at line 408 and shifts on uart_clk at line 410; rx_engine.state selects idle and receive behavior at line 418 and leaves idle on the sampled "01" pattern at lines 424-425; rx_engine.baudcnt and rx_engine.bitcnt are loaded at lines 422-423 and updated at lines 432-436 and 433. The receive operate flow depends on these stored states for start detection, bit timing, and end-of-frame detection at lines 439-441, establishing integrity and conditional availability.

conceptual assets.concept: Received serial frame data being captured
conceptual assets.reasoning: uart_rxd_i enters the entity at line 408, and during receive state rx_engine.sreg shifts sampled bits in at line 434. The assembled byte then feeds rx_fifo.wdata at line 305 and is committed with rx_engine.done at line 306; later bus readback uses FIFO output at line 217, but that bus exit is excluded as transport and the FIFO storage is in a sub-unit. Integrity matters because corruption changes received bytes; availability is conditional on ctrl.enable, start detection, and sampling timing (lines 417, 424-425, 430-436).

irq_tx_o is registered from ctrl.enable and the configured TX FIFO conditions at lines 270-272, and irq_rx_o is registered from ctrl.enable and the configured RX FIFO conditions at lines 315-318. Under the module-boundary delivery assumption, integrity requires these outputs to present exactly the qualifying conditions the RTL defines; availability is established while ctrl.enable='1' and the selected FIFO conditions hold.

rx_engine.over is cleared on reset and when ctrl.enable='0' (lines 456 and 459) and set when a receive write occurs while the RX FIFO is full `(rx_fifo.we = '1') and (rx_fifo.free = '0')` at line 461. It is reported on the control/status readback bit at line 214, though that transport exit is excluded from structural reporting. Integrity matters because corruption misreports whether received data was dropped; availability is established because the flag is retained until reset or disable.

The rtr_control process updates uart_rtsn_o each clock. When ctrl.hwfc_en='1', the port is driven '1' if ctrl.enable='0' or rx_fifo.half='1' and '0' otherwise (lines 472-477); when ctrl.hwfc_en='0', it is forced '0' (line 480). The operate flow with an external peer depends on this decision being delivered exactly as defined, and availability is established whenever the clocked process runs.
